findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: 'Resolved' leaves no room for an earlier finding the planner rebutted with evidence, so a mistaken earlier major can keep forcing rounds up to the cap.
findings.evidence: Bullet A reads '...check that each earlier blocker and major finding was resolved in the plan under review; raise any that was not again at its earlier severity.' Decision 3 shows each earlier round's answer as the next plan's decisions, which is where a planner rebuts a finding. Read literally, A tells the critic to raise a rebutted finding again at its earlier severity. `plan_verdict` (run/mod.rs:364) then turns that into revise. A wrong round-2 major could therefore repeat every round until the 5-round stop, which is the failure the request wants fewer of. By my hand count A is 159 bytes, and 22 bytes of slack remain under the frame bound. Fix: Change A to '...was resolved, or rebutted with evidence, in the plan under review; ...' (+24 bytes, slightly over the slack; trim 'finding ' from A to fit). Or use '...was resolved or answered in the plan under review...' (+12 bytes). Update the criterion 3 pin to match.

findings.summary: The SHA-256 literal fails on any later edit to the critic brief's fixed tail text (history section, soundness section, NO_CHANGE_PLAN_RULE), not only on changes to this section.
findings.evidence: The digest covers everything from '## History file' to the end, including shared constants that other jobs edit. Checks (a)-(e) already pin the structure by hand-written text. The plan's own risks list this. Fix: Optional: say in the test's failure message which constants the tail embeds, so a later job knows that updating the literal is expected.

summary: Round 3 plan. I checked its main claims against the snapshot and they hold. `critic_brief` (planner.rs:185-210) prints only the current plan. `CriticInputs` is built in one production place (planning.rs:353), and a grep finds no other constructor. `end_round` adds the plan and its critique together (planning.rs:483-484). The two stop paths (312-313, 350) end planning. A mechanical pass returns without adding anything (251-269). So pairing each critique with its plan by round number in `closing` is sound. The record structs derive PartialEq (records/plan.rs), so the `Item` comparison compiles as described. I counted the two critic.md bullets by hand at 159 and 280 bytes, matching the plan's 439. That stays under the frame bound of fewer than 900 estimated tokens (lib.rs:570). The plan correctly sees that `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` forces the one-number edit to docs/system-facts.md:29. No other file pins 1056 except a historical CHANGELOG line. D188 is the last decision, so D189 is free. The test helpers the plan relies on exist as described: `planning_script` repeats the last queue entry, `revising_critique` has a `findings[0].summary`, `critique_of` sets location 'demonstrations', and the wrapper pattern is at job_plan.rs:1054-1061. Each demonstration runs through the real path (`Athena::go` → `plan_round` → `critic_round` → `critic_brief`) and would fail on today's code. Bullet A (re-raise unresolved earlier findings at their earlier severity) together with the unchanged `plan_verdict` keeps an ignored major forcing another round. Bullet B limits only new majors, as the request asks. I found only minor issues. Bullet A's word 'resolved' may make the critic re-raise an earlier finding that the planner rebutted with evidence, which could prolong the loop. The tail-digest test is brittle against later edits to the critic brief's fixed text; the plan already lists this as a risk. Athena's own finding about docs/system-facts.md is answered by the plan's reasoning that the budgets test forces the edit.
